Connections

Name an external API or PostgreSQL database once, with its credential kept in the vault, for app steps and Script Library scripts to call — every call stays under the connection's base URL and never reaches this node or cloud metadata.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.script_library
📍 WherePlugin Studio (first level of the sidebar) → Connections (URL /studio/?pane=connections; a connection is /studio/connections/<id>)

What is it?#

A connection is an external system named once — an HTTP API or a PostgreSQL database — with its credential, so that app steps and form lists can use it without anyone typing the credential again.

What does it do?#

Kind Settings Authentication
HTTP API Base URL, TLS verification against the trust store, timeout None · Basic (user + password) · Bearer token · API key in a named header · OAuth2 client credentials (client id, secret, token URL, scope) · Session login (user + password posted to a login path under the base URL, the session cookie reused; one new login on a 401)
PostgreSQL Host, port, database, user, TLS verification, timeout Password
  • Every call stays under the base URL. A step's path is joined to it; an absolute URL, //, .. or a backslash is refused, and a redirect comes back as the answer — it is never followed. A step cannot set the Authorization header, the API-key header, Host or Cookie.
  • The secret is write-only. The page can replace or clear it and never shows it. It is kept in the vault, or encrypted with SATOM's key, by the vault mode, and the vault's migrate and remove local copies actions cover it. It is redacted out of every error message.
  • Where a connection may point. SATOM resolves the host once and refuses it when any of its addresses is loopback, link-local (cloud metadata lives at 169.254.169.254), multicast, unspecified, reserved, or an address of this node — the node's metrics store, cache and web server listen there without authentication. Internal addresses (10.x, 172.16–31.x, 192.168.x) are allowed. The request goes to the address that was checked, with the name kept as Host and TLS server name, so a DNS answer that changes in between changes nothing. The OAuth2 token URL (https only) and a PostgreSQL host get the same check, on every call: app steps, form lists filled from an API, Test, scripts.
  • PostgreSQL queries use %(name)s parameters and run in a READ ONLY transaction unless the app step ticks Allow writes. The connection is always encrypted: TLS verification on checks the server certificate against the trust store (verify-full); off encrypts without the check (require). A server without TLS is refused, so the password never travels in clear.
  • Test tries a GET (or a read-only SQL statement) and shows the answer. Type a JSON path — a.b[0].c picks one value, items[*].name collects a field from every item — to see what a step would keep.
  • In app packages a connection never carries its secret. An exported app writes its HTTP connections without one; a package connection with a non-empty password, secret, token, api_key or client_secret is refused, and so is a PostgreSQL connection. The import page asks for the secret of each connection it creates and stores it here like any other (an existing connection keeps its own). An app that uses a connection still without its secret shows connection … has no secret yet and cannot be published. See The import page.

ℹ️Note

The credential is never in a script's hands. A Script Library script calls the connections it declares (script editor → Settings → Connections) with satom_script.connection("crm").get("/tickets") — or .query("SELECT …", {...}) on PostgreSQL. The scripts runner makes the call outside the sandbox, adds the credential, and hands back the answer. A connection with a secret needs the vault: the run receives a single-use wrapped token, never the secret on disk.

Pinned to an API version#

An HTTP connection can be pinned to a published version in the API Catalog (API version on the connection page). Then app steps and scripts reach only that version's endpoints and can call them by id — connection("inv").op("getHost", {"id": 7}). Moving it to another version names the app steps that would lose an endpoint and asks you to confirm.

Safeguards#

  • Changing where a connection points clears its secret: the scheme, host or port of the base URL, the authentication, the API-key header, the token URL, the user or TLS verification (PostgreSQL: host, port, database, user, TLS). The page says so; type the secret again. Otherwise whoever may edit a connection could point it at their own server and press Test to receive the token. Name, description, timeout and the path under the same host keep it.
  • An echoed credential is masked in every answer — the secret, the Authorization value, the Basic base64 form, an OAuth2 token — before a step, a script or an operator sees it.
  • The other HA node is refused like this node. A path may not carry an encoded ., / or \ (%2e, %2f, %5c); the query string is re-encoded.
  • One call, one deadline: twice the timeout plus 5 seconds.
  • PostgreSQL runs one statement (extended protocol), read-only twice (transaction and session) unless writes are allowed; results stop at 8 MiB; a server asking for the password in clear is refused (libpq 16+). Use a read-only role on the remote database: that is the real boundary.

Permissions#

Action Permission
Create, edit, test and delete connections; set their secret studio.script_library

How to use#

  1. Plugin Studio (first level of the sidebar) → Connections → New connection: a name, an id and the kind.
  2. Fill in the settings and Save.
  3. Under Secret, type the password, token, API key or client secret and Replace.
  4. Under Test, type a path (HTTP) or a query (PostgreSQL) and run it.

Troubleshooting#

"a path is relative to the connection's base URL; an absolute URL is refused"#

A step (or a form list) sent a full URL. Give a path under the base URL, or create another connection for the other host.

HTTP 3xx in a test#

The server redirected. Redirects are never followed: point the base URL at the final address.

"no secret is stored for …"#

The authentication needs a secret and none is set, or the vault holds it and could not be read (the message says which). Set it again under Secret.

"… resolves to …, a loopback address of this node; a connection never dials it"#

The base URL, the token URL or the PostgreSQL host points at this node itself, at cloud metadata or at another forbidden range (the message names it). Use the address of the real service. A name that answers with several addresses is refused when any one of them is forbidden.

PostgreSQL: "SSL … certificate verify failed" or "server does not support SSL"#

With TLS verification on, the server certificate must be signed by a CA in the trust store and match the host name. A server without TLS is refused in both modes. Add the CA, or untick TLS verification to encrypt without the check.

A script says "connection … is not declared by this script"#

Tick the connection under Settings → Connections in the script editor and save; a published version keeps the connections it was published with.

A script run fails with "… a script receives connection secrets only from the vault"#

The connection has a secret and no vault holds it. Configure Settings → Vault (or run its migrate) so the run can get a single-use wrapped token.

A connection cannot be deleted#

An app uses it, or a script declares it; the message names them. Remove it from them first.
